intuition.title: Water dispersibility
intuition.text: The authors use MPA exchange to disperse the hydrophobic synthesis product in water and report dispersion for up to one month. Exchange conditions and quantitative stability criteria are not supplied.

intuition.title: Molecular recognition and optical readout
intuition.text: The authors design thymine mismatches so Hg(II)-mediated coordination brings QD and Au probes close enough for fluorescence quenching. This is their NSET interpretation; the paper does not supply an atomistic interface model.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Results and mechanism discussion

intuition.title: River-matrix limitations
intuition.text: The source reports a higher detection limit and lower initial fluorescence in river water than in pure PBS, attributing the difference to environmental substances.

intuition.title: Proposed applications
intuition.text: The authors propose on-site monitoring and future multi-ion detection using differently emitting QDs excited by one light source. These remain outlooks, not a demonstrated multianalyte device in this paper.

scopeLabel: Five supplied main pages. All displayed original figures describe the downstream optical assay; they are not TEM or XPS. Size values are reported in main text, while underlying SI microscopy remains unreviewed. Independent scientific audit passed; visual refinements pending.

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

general_background.title: Electron transfer from a reductant
general_background.summary: A reducing agent can supply electrons that change the oxidation state of a precursor. Coordination and competing reactions affect how that electron transfer contributes to particle formation.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
